thread:
micah: Kicking off SFO region account + network wiring for new GPU fleet. Target: SFO (sfo3) H100/4-slot nodes for dedicated pool. I'll create the project skeleton and request quotas, need quick sanity check on CIDR plan and peering to prod-hub.

taylor: Thanks. Are we using host/shared VPC or standalone project-VPC? Also what subnet sizing are we thinking for gpu nodes vs control plane?

sasha: Prefer host project with Shared VPC (prod-hub). Keeps routing simple for observability and egress. For subnets: cluster node subnets /21 for GPU pools, control plane /24. Avoid overlapping with existing 10.240.0.0/16 ranges.

micah: Plan: project id = redwood-sfo3-gpu-01 (temporary). Use Shared VPC peered into prod-hub via VPC peering (no NAT). CIDR proposal: 10.248.0.0/20 for region (split into AZ subnets). Example split:

```
10.248.0.0/22  -> sfo3-gpu-az-a (nodes)
10.248.4.0/22  -> sfo3-gpu-az-b (nodes)
10.248.8.0/24  -> sfo3-controlplane
10.248.9.0/24  -> sfo3-services
```

Want feedback before I land the terraform.

jia: Quick checklist to validate before handoff:
- Billing enabled on project
- Org IAM roles: infra-service-sa, gpu-provisioner
- Enable Private Google Access for node subnets
- Firewall: allow 10250, 22 from prod-hub, node -> container registry
- VPC peering routes published to prod-hub
- Cloud NAT only if egress to internet required (considering cost)
- GPU quotas: compute.googleapis.com/accelerator?type=nvidia-h100 = request x250
- Regional static ranges for internal LB
- Monitoring agents & Stackdriver sinks

alex: On cost: NAT per-AZ + egress can add ~$800/mo per AZ. If we can do Private Google Access + Artifact Registry access via peering, we can avoid NAT and save. Also reserved capacity for Dedicated would shift pricing—ops to evaluate with finance.

sasha: Inventory note: SFO zone B has historically lower H100 availability. We should request quota across two AZs and mark autoscaler to prefer AZ A/C in rollout. Also set capacity fallback to T4 for burst if H100 not available in emergency.

micah: Will file quota ticket with cloud provider and create infra ticket in linear. infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-4872 for project creation and GPU quota requests.

infra-bot: Ticket INFRA-4872 created by micah. Links: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/INFRA-4872/sfo3-gpu-project-setup

taylor: For terraform: I'll add a workspace `sfo3-gpu` and a `modules/hosted_shared_vpc` call. Use naming convention `redwood-region-role-idx` for subnets. PR will include TF var overrides for project id and CIDRs.

micah: I'll add a short runbook section in infra/runbooks/region-onboard.md with the validation checklist (jia's list) and a command snippet for quota polling.

sasha: One more: ensure KMS key policy allows customer-managed key usage from the project if we deploy Dedicated nodes with encrypted images.

micah: Ack. Handoff plan: micah -> create project + open PR -> taylor iterate terraform -> sasha request quotas and availability check -> jia run validation checklist and sign off -> micah merge and assign Dedicated pool request to sales-eng for capacity commit.

taylor: Got it. I'll start the TF scaffold in a branch `infra/sfo3-gpu-setup` and ping here when PR is up.

micah: ETA: aim to have project skeleton + quota requests in 48 hours. Posting updates in this thread.

alex: FYI I'll loop in finance for a rough cost projection for 250 H100-equivalent devices (dedicated vs on-demand) once quota request is in.

taylor: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1127 (draft) - includes VPC, subnets, service accounts, basic firewall. Still needs NAT decision and peering module.

jia: Once PR is ready I'll run validation steps and attach results. Minimal test: create one GPU instance, run a short perf job, check metrics exported to monitoring.

micah: Solid. Thanks all. Will update thread with cloud provider response and quota ticket updates. :thumbsup:
